newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa says will build a million homes by 1999.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa says will build a million homes by 1999.

text.p: South Africa is on track to deliver on the promise made during the 1994 elections to build one million houses by 1999, Housing Minister Sankie Mthembi-Mahanyele said on Wednesday.
The government has been under fire for the slow pace of building since the general elections.
Only 30,000 houses have been built so far in a country where more than a fifth of all South Africans live in a shack or a hut and nearly half have neither electricity nor a modern toilet.
"We are confindent that this year we are going to deliver more and more houses. That is, by 1999 we will have delivered the one million houses (promised)," Mthembi-Mahanyele told a news conference.
The government's subsidy scheme for the low-income group had been well used with 380,000 applications processed so far.
Mthembi-Mahanyele said that by June this year the government would have processed 500,000 subsidy applications. She declined to say how many houses this would translate into by the end of the year.

She said the housing delivery process had been streamlined to reduce the number of people needed to approve a subsidy and the time for construction of houses. The quality of houses had also been improved.

Government was looking into ways of improving delivery in rural areas which lagged behind urban areas, while housing budget rollovers in the provinces should be a thing of the past as provinces were now spending ahead of their budgets.
The Gauteng Province around Johannesburg was ahead in delivery -- but the Eastern Cape, North West and Northern Provinces were struggling, she said.
